note: Light weekend edition. The Anthropic IPO and OpenAI's agent research numbers were covered earlier this week, so they're skipped here.

top.title: Gartner: 91% of executives expect AI to do a quarter of the CMO's job within two years
top.summary: A Gartner survey of 282 senior executives found 91% expect AI to take on at least 25% of CMO responsibilities in two years, and one in five expect it to cover half or more. Gartner says routine work moves to AI while growth bets made on incomplete data stay with people.
top.why: This is the budget-holder view that will shape marketing headcount next cycle, so a task-level map of what PMM workflows automate versus where people decide is the evidence to bring to that conversation.

top.title: OneTrust's math: a $100M AI case keeps about $30M in production, $51M with better governance
top.summary: OneTrust modeled how pilot value erodes once you apply realistic reliability, adoption and realization rates, then subtract run costs and expected losses. Modestly better numbers from standard intake, reusable controls and monitoring raise retained value from about $30M to $51M.
top.why: A ready-made frame for reporting PMM workflow ROI honestly: discount time-saved claims by adoption and reliability, and show governance as the lever that raises what you keep.

top.title: Perplexity Computer now writes and updates its own skills from past sessions
top.summary: Perplexity's Brain system watches each user's past sessions and turns repeated work into skills it builds and revises on its own.
top.why: Self-editing skills cut maintenance work but break versioning and review, so if this pattern reaches Claude or Copilot you'll want a rule that auto-generated skill changes get diffed and approved before teams use them.

try_this.title: Split one PMM role into AI does it, AI drafts and I decide, and only me
try_this.how: Copy the O*NET task list for marketing managers into a sheet, tag each task with one of the three labels, and add last month's hours. The 'AI drafts, I decide' rows are your shortlist for the next workflows to build, with a human-review step already defined.

workflows.title: Gemini API adds Tool Retrieval, picking the right function from a large registry
workflows.summary: Developers register many functions and the Gemini API finds and runs the relevant one based on the request, instead of loading every tool into each call.
workflows.why: The same problem shows up as PMM agents gain connectors and skills; on-demand tool loading keeps context lean and behavior predictable.

workflows.title: Replit: 32 agents beat one on a speedup task, but only when work split cleanly
workflows.summary: A team of 32 agents reached an 18.9x speedup versus 3.7x for a single agent in two hours, using more compute. Gains depended on separable tasks and a shared coordination board.
workflows.why: A useful test before going multi-agent in marketing: if the job can't be split into independent pieces with a shared status board, one agent is likely the better design.

workflows.title: Google Cloud's five patterns for orchestrating agents without making them worse
workflows.summary: The cookbook covers splitting work, verification steps, parallel agents, model councils and specialist reviewers, plus when a multi-agent setup actually beats one agent.
workflows.why: Specialist reviewers and verification steps map directly to a PMM content pipeline, such as a separate claims-check or brand-voice reviewer after drafting.

governance.title: Attacker swapped a hosted model for a jailbreak-prone copy for two days
governance.summary: Prime Intellect says an attacker replaced its DeepSeek endpoint from November 8 to 10 with a copy that refused only 1 in 100 jailbreak prompts. Developers spotted it through OpenRouter and are now asking for model attestation.
governance.why: A concrete case for Security reviews: approved-model lists only help if you can confirm which model a third-party endpoint actually serves.

governance.title: Canva lets users switch off its generative AI features
governance.summary: New settings disable Magic Write, Magic Design, Dream Lab, Canva Code and similar tools, and a separate preference reduces AI-generated templates in search.
governance.why: Gives brand or Legal a simple control if certain assets must stay free of generated content.

governance.title: 53% of creatives have used AI on important client work without saying so
governance.summary: Envato surveyed 1,033 creatives: 87% use AI at work and 58% daily, but few earn more from it. Taste and judgment ranked as the most valuable skills and prompting ranked last.
governance.why: Undisclosed use is the norm, so agency and freelancer contracts need an explicit AI disclosure clause.

competitive.title: Docker repositions as a trusted runtime for AI agents
competitive.summary: Docker's rebrand adds the line 'Run on Trust' and positions it as secure execution infrastructure for autonomous agents as well as apps.
competitive.why: Another infrastructure vendor is claiming the 'safe place to run agents' message, which overlaps with how orchestration platforms pitch governed agent execution.

competitive.title: Vercel Board: a message board where agents claim tasks and share context
competitive.summary: Vercel released an experimental board where AI agents pick up tasks, post updates and pass context to each other.
competitive.why: A lightweight take on agent coordination from a developer platform; worth tracking as a signal of how developers may handle multi-agent work without a full orchestration engine.

measurement.title: Stripe's method for scoring coding agents on realistic integration jobs
measurement.summary: Stripe built an eval that uses a role-playing agent to give coding agents realistic, well-specified scenarios, then grades how well the resulting integrations follow best practice.
measurement.why: The role-played requester plus a quality rubric is a pattern you could borrow to score PMM workflow outputs consistently.

measurement.title: A four-question audit for whether a feature should use AI at all
measurement.summary: The audit asks whether AI cuts total effort including verification, beats the current method, lets users catch errors, and keeps their checking skills intact over time.
measurement.why: Works as an intake filter for workflow requests, so you build only where verification costs don't eat the time saved.

enablement.title: Anthropic opens a 9.5-hour Forward Deployed Engineer learning path
enablement.summary: Anthropic published a free course path covering what the forward deployed engineer role involves when rolling out Claude.
enablement.why: The deployment and adoption modules could inform how you run internal AI champion or concierge programs.
